bug_semantics: PhpSpreadsheet's OLE/XLS reader walks attacker-controlled SAT/SSAT sector chains in OLERead::read() with only the OLE end-of-chain sentinel (sector id -2). There is no visited-set, maximum chain length, EOF bound, or rejection of self-loops, so a 1 KiB malformed .xls that maps SAT sector 0 to itself makes the small-block-depot builder append the same sector data forever until PHP memory_limit is exhausted (CWE-400/CWE-835). Pre-fix sink at src/PhpSpreadsheet/Shared/OLERead.php:138-146 (parent of 85f2556): while ($sbdBlock != -2) { $this->smallBlockChain .= substr($this->data, $pos, 4 * $bbs); $sbdBlock = self::getInt4d($this->bigBlockChain, $sbdBlock * 4); }. The same unguarded while ($block != -2) walks exist in getStream() small-block and big-block extraction and in readData(). Reachable from Reader\XlsBase::canRead() (OLERead::read() at XlsBase.php:161-164), from Xls::loadOLE(), and therefore from IOFactory autodetection of untrusted uploads. CVE-2026-59933 is PUBLISHED on CVE.org (GitHub_M, 2026-07-28); GHSA-xh5m-36r6-47m3 withdrawn_at is null.

Classes/PHPExcel/Shared/OLERead.php:146-156 already implemented while ($sbdBlock != -2) { fill smallBlockChain from the sector; $sbdBlock = $this->bigBlockChain[$sbdBlock]; } with no cycle detection, and Classes/PHPExcel/Reader/Excel5.php:475-480 already called OLERead::read() from canRead(). That commit has no parent tree, so the lines are absent before it; finer CodePlex SVN members are not reconstructable in this clone. 2012-11-26 b98f27f4a7fb8f95546480c83779d72cf46837ea (Mark Baker, parent d8debd09665f0fc7439945c029dd2727f2e26f38) is a performance refactor that replaced the array fill with $this->smallBlockChain .= substr(...) — the exact memory-bomb lines quoted in the advisory — but the parent still had the same unbounded while ($sbdBlock != -2) walk, so it is not the BIC. Later PSR-2, namespace, and phpstan commits only restyled or moved the file to src/PhpSpreadsheet/Shared/OLERead.php.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: GHSA-xh5m-36r6-47m3 / CVE-2026-59933 is a real, published DoS. OLERead follows file-controlled SAT/SSAT next-sector pointers until -2 with no cycle detection, so a self-loop inflates smallBlockChain (and the later stream walks) until memory exhaustion. This is reachable from canRead() as well as load, matching the advisory PoC stack (XlsBase::canRead -> OLERead::read). The 2026-07-11 commit 85f2556 is the direct master-line patch (catchLoop visited set) and is in 5.8.1 but not 5.8.0; matching catchLoop backports land in the other patched tags. BIC: git log -L / -S / --diff-filter=A on OLERead.php show the unbounded while ($sbdBlock != -2) chain walk was first written in this public history at root import 509f27e5 (PHPExcel OLERead.php:146-156 plus Excel5::canRead already invoking it). That object has no parent; parent-tree absence was verified via empty %P, failed 509f27e5^, and rev-list --max-parents=0. It is a git-svn snapshot, not a reconstructable squash of public git members, so it is the smallest surviving first-write. The 2012 Mark Baker performance change rewrote storage from arrays to string concatenation (the advisory's quoted lines) but is a refactor of the already-unbounded walk, not the BIC. AI judgment is from the BIC commit object only: 2010 human git-svn import by Maarten Balliauw with no AI/co-author/bot trailers, therefore NOT_AI.
